Course Description
Probability calculus; random variables, their probability distributions and expected values; t, F and chi-square sampling distributions; estimation; testing of hypothesis; and regression analysis with applications.

Midterm: There will be one midterm approximately halfway through the semester. Details will be provided in class.

title: STAT 380
text:
Random Variables
A random variable (RV) is a real – valued function defined over a sample space. A RV assigns a value to each outcome in the sample space.
Typically, capital letters at the END of the alphabet are used to denote a RV.
The corresponding lower case letter is then used to denote a specific value.

text:
Joint probability distribution
Up until this point, we’ve been looking at just one random variable at a time. Often, we are interested in the simultaneous outcomes of several random variables
Examples:
For heart patients, we might be interested in heart rate, blood pressure (this could be broken down into systolic and diastolic), and cholesterol (again, could break down to HDL and LDL).
For college applicants, we may want to look at high school GPA, class rank, and ACT/SAT score.
The white blood cell count for patients at times: 0, 1, and 2 hours after a medicine is administered.

title: In-class Counting Problems
text:
Chess is a popular game with a seemingly infinite number of distinct games. For the following problems, we will examine the first two moves of the game. Assume that all moves are randomly chosen and that the players are not using strategy.

Each player has 16 pieces, consisting of 8 pawns, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, 1 queen, and 1 king. White plays first with the options of moving any pawn 1 or 2 spaces forward, or the knight forward 2 spaces and to either the left of right 1 space. After white moves one piece, then black has the same options for their first move.

How many distinct board positions are there after white plays their first move?
How many distinct board positions are there after black plays their first move?
What is the probability that white plays one of the pawns in front of the king or queen?
Given that white played a knight in their first move, what is the probability that black plays a pawn?
Is black playing a pawn independent of white playing a knight for their first move?


Now consider white’s first three moves, and assume that each move is valid (i.e., do not consider black’s potential moves).

If white’s first three moves involved moving three different pawns one space forward, how many white pawn configurations are there? (i.e., played pawn a3, b3, and d3).


For moves 4 and 5, white has the options to play using 8 pawns, 2 knights, 1 bishop, 1 queen, and 1 king. Again, assume that each piece can be validly played and that move 4 does change what pieces could be played in move 5.

How many piece pairs could white play for their next two moves, assuming that the order does not matter?

For each problem, you must show your work in order to receive credit. No credit will be received if you do not show your work. Following question 2, if at least 3 women and at least 2 men are required, how many different committees are possible?
Suppose that two cards are drawn without replacement from a standard 52-card deck (no jokers). text:
The final project for this course consists of two components where you will find and describe a probability distribution that has not been discussed in class (examples). title: Final Project
text:
Write-up
Due date: end of the scheduled final exam for the course
The written report should be 4-6 pages and contain the following sections:

Introduction: describe your distribution, the type of data it describes, history, etc.
Mathematical description: provide the mathematical definition of the probability function (you do not need to derive anything), as well as restrictions on the support of the RV and its parameters. Describe the mean and variance of the function (again, you do not need to derive this). Additionally, include a plot of the pmf/pdf, as well as how it changes with different parameters (e.g., the exponential distribution with \(\beta=1,2,3\))
R Implementation: describe how to use this probability function in R (e.g., qnorm(), pnorm(), packages, etc.). If this function is not implemented in R, describe the process of how to write these functions for your distribution.
Applications: describe 2-3 practical applications where your probability function would be used.
Example: provide a completed example of a practical application of the distribution from a published source. If you would like, you may also fit this distribution to data of your own choosing.

title: Final Project
text:
Presentation
Due date: last week of classes
During the last week of classes, you and your group will present your distribution to the class (approximately 4 groups/day). Your presentation should be between 7 and 10 minutes, and include the opportunities for the class to ask questions. At the minimum, you must include the following sections:

Introduction (including mathematical description)
R Implementation
Example

To ensure that each group has enough time to present, a portion of your grade is allocated to keeping your presentation to under 10 minutes.
In addition to presenting your distribution, you are also responsible for listening to your peers present. On Canvas, there is a quiz with one question per group.

\]

Create a function in R called my_dt to calculate \(f(x)\) at a given \(x\) and \(\nu\).

title: Handout 2 Problems
text:
Suppose that you have a perfectly shuffled deck of 52 playing cards and draw 5 cards.

How many ways could you get a royal flush (same suit for 10, J, Q, K, A)?
How many ways could you get a straight flush without having a royal flush (same suit for sequence of 5 cards)?
How many ways could you get a four of a kind?
How many ways could you get a 3 of a kind and a pair?
How many ways could you get a 3 of a kind without a pair?
How many ways could you get a hand without any pairs, three of kind, or four of a kind?



How many possible ways could you receive your five cards?
How would you calculate probabilities for 1-6?
